triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The composition's fentanyl branch applied the heading 9903.01.24 / note 2(u) 10% additional duty only to China-origin entries, omitting the Hong Kong half of the provision's stated scope ("products of China and Hong Kong"), so HK-origin entries were assigned a 0 fentanyl rate.
triage.triage_notes: Single module in the commit (chunk covers all of module_files). Provision WAS read through the pinned corpus release: us/statute/hts/chapter-99/page-176 note 2(u) reads "For the purposes of heading 9903.01.24, products of China and Hong Kong entered for consumption... shall be subject to an additional 10% ad valorem rate of duty", confirming the scope. Verified with git show that the parent commit d168b7f5 contains zero occurrences of 'hong_kong' anywhere in composition.yaml, while the post-fix file has 3 (new rule + both widened formulas). The file is `module.kind: composition` but is a rulespec/v1 module carrying real rules, versions and formulas (the commit itself calls it the "merged composition"), so I treated it as a rule module rather than not_a_rule_module. The diff also changes a rationale comment block and adds one condition proof atom (verbatim note 2(u) entry-date clause) on ieepa_component_rate_with_declared_exceptions; those are provenance/documentation, mechanical alongside the substantive scope fix. Non-module files in the commit (composition.test.yaml with 3 new HK cases, the encoding manifest, oracle-coverage-pending.yaml ledger +1 for the new judgment output) are consistent with the stated fix and change nothing else. Kind alternative: this could also be read as unrepresented_clause (the HK half of the source clause was missing and the fix adds it); I chose wrong_entity_or_scope because the commit and PR both describe it as a scope/geography defect ("Scope defect in merged composition") and the correction is to the geographic population the branch fires for. PR #1198 body notes a follow-up panel re-classification landing harness-side in axiom-oracles (lane E), not in this repo. No PR reviews or review comments exist on the merged PR.
triage.verifier_justification:
The diff changes encoded meaning in exactly the way the first reader described: both `ieepa_component_rate` and `ieepa_component_rate_with_declared_exceptions` fentanyl branches go from `(if origin_is_china: ...` to `(if origin_is_china or origin_is_hong_kong: ...`, plus a new `origin_is_hong_kong` derived judgment (`country_of_origin == "HK"`) — formulas and origin scope, not bookkeeping. The pinned corpus text of U.S. note 2(u) (us/statute/hts/chapter-99/page-176) reads "For the purposes of heading 9903.01.24, products of China and Hong Kong entered for consumption ... shall be subject to an additional 10% ad valorem rate of duty", so the pre-fix encoding covered only half the provision's stated geography. This is not uncla
imed new coverage: the pre-fix composition already priced HK entries through its general origin cascade (reciprocal/baseline `else` branches, no `HK` string anywhere in the pre file), so an HK entry got a computed fentanyl component of 0 — a wrong value for an in-scope population. Kind holds: the defect is an under-inclusive geographic population, which is wrong_entity_or_scope; unrepresented_clause fits worse because the added disjunct is the second half of the provision's scope phrase rather than a separate exception or carve-out, and polarity_or_logic fits worse because no boolean was inverted or mis-combined.
triage.verifier_notes: Verified against the pinned release (corpus commit d9d6fba0, provision file 2026-08-01-usitc-hts-2026-rev3-notes.jsonl line 186): note 2(u) scope is verbatim "products of China and Hong Kong", and the new proof atom's excerpt is verbatim from that record. Pre-file check (git show d168b7f5:...composition.yaml) shows no "HK" / "hong" token anywhere and origin judgments only for CN/CA/MX/KR/VN/ZA/GB/BR/RU/etc., confirming HK fell to the fentanyl `else: 0`. Post-file has both fentanyl gates widened (lines 2419, 2565); the remaining `origin_is_china`-only gates at 2804-2806 are Section 301 list rates, a different provision, so the fix is complete for note 2(u). No period issue: the new judgment's effective_from 2026-02-15 matches the branch version window, and the note's own Nov 10 2025 entry-date clause predates the composition's coverage. Non-module files in the commit (companion tests, manifest, oracle-coverage ledger) are consistent with the fidelity fix, not the substance of it.
